items.actClause: AN ACT to require the commissioner of education to survey, examine and report about school district compliance with physical education instruction requirements in elementary grades in public schools
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S3344

TITLE OF BILL:

An act to require the commissioner of education to survey, examine and
report about school district compliance with physical education
instruction requirements in elementary grades in public schools

PURPOSE:

The goal of this bill is to ensure that school districts comply with
physical instruction requirements in elementary and secondary grades
by requiring the commissioner of education to survey, examine, and
report about such compliance.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: This section requires the commissioner of education to
submit a report to the governor and legislature regarding schools that
do not have facilities available for physical education use, schools
that do not have teachers employed or designated to teach physical
education, schools that do not provide legally required class time for
physical education, and schools that are not in compliance with
physical education requirements, along with analysis and explanation
of this information and identification of the amps that the education
department is taking to ensure compliance with physical education
requirements in elementary and secondary grades.

Section 2: This lists the effective date.

JUSTIFICATION:

This bill follows a public hearing that was held in 2003 by the
Assembly Standing Committee on Education regarding compliance with
required physical education classes. At the hearing, teachers,
principals, and education advocates-testified about instances in which
schools were not meeting physical education requirements. In addition,
a survey sponsored by NYSUT found that teachers did not believe school
districts to be complying with requirements, and a 2011 audit by the
NYC comptroller found that no city elementary schools were in
compliance with state physical education requirements. SED too did an
audit of a limited number of school districts in 2008 and found that
districts generally were not complying with regulations.

Schools' compliance with state regulations is essential to the health
and well being of New York's children. A lack of physical activity is
engendering higher obesity rates for children, manifesting itself in
higher rates of diabetes, asthma, high blood pressure, and other
pulmonary diseases. All of these indicators demonstrate the declining
health of our young. Many studies show that unhealthy lifestyles in
youth lead to much poorer health outcomes in adulthood. Regulations
regarding physical education serve to ensure that students receive the
amount of physical activity and learning needed to maintain their
health.

By requiring the commissioner of education to report to the
legislature and the governor regarding compliance with physical


education requirements, and outlining the steps that SED is taking to
increase compliance, we can ensure that schools are giving elementary
and secondary students the physical education that they need to stay
healthy.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2014 - S.7715 Referred to Education / A.8592 Referred to Ways and
Means

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect immediately.

B.actClause: AN ACT to require school district compliance with physical education instruction requirements in elementary grades in public schools to be reported to the department of education
B.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S3344B

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to require school district compliance with physical education
instruction requirements in elementary grades in public schools to be
reported to the department of education

 PURPOSE :

This bill requires school districts to report to the department of
education and thereby ensures compliance with physical instruction
requirements in elementary schools

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 requires the commissioner to create a procedure by which
school district compliance with physical education instruction
requirements as required by law and regulation in elementary grades in
all public schools is reported to the department by school districts.
Section 2 is effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :

This bill follows a public hearing that was held in 2003 by the
Assembly Standing Committee on Education regarding compliance with
required physical education classes. At the hearing, teachers,
principals, and education advocates-testified about instances in which
schools were not meeting physical education requirements. In addition,
a survey sponsored by NYSUT found that teachers did not believe school
districts to be complying with requirements, and a 2011 audit by the
NYC comptroller found that no city elementary schools were in
compliance with state physical education requirements. SED too did an
audit of a limited number of school districts in 2008 and found that
districts generally were not complying with regulations.

Schools' compliance with state regulations is essential to the health
and well-being of New York's children. A lack of physical activity is
leading to higher obesity rates for children and manifesting itself in
higher rates of diabetes, asthma, high blood pressure and other
pulmonary diseases. All of these indicators demonstrate the declining
health of our young. Many studies show that unhealthy lifestyles in
youth lead to much poorer health outcomes in adulthood. Regulations
regarding physical education serve to ensure that students receive the
amount of physical activity and learning needed to maintain their
health.

By requiring the commissioner of education to establish a procedure
whereby school report about compliance and efforts to remedy
non-compliance, New York State can ensure that schools are giving
elementary students the physical education that they need to stay
healthy.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2015 - S.3344 - Referred to Education / A.3880 - Reported to Ways and
Means;
2014 - S.7715 Referred to Education / A.8592 Referred to Ways and
Means

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 268

TO THE SENATE:

I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:

Senate Bill Number 3344-B, entitled:

    "AN  ACT  to require school district compliance with physical educa-
      tion instruction  requirements  in  elementary  grades  in  public
      schools to be reported to the department of education"

    NOT APPROVED

  This  bill  would establish a detailed one-time reporting protocol for
public school districts to report their  compliance  with  the  physical
education  requirements  for  elementary grades. School districts not in
compliance must prepare a corrective action plan  for  approval  by  the
school  district's  board  of  education and will be listed on the State
Education Department's website.

  I fully support the intent of this  bill,  which  is  to  ensure  that
State-mandated  physical  education  classes  are meeting their intended
goal of improving student health and reducing  incidences  of  childhood
obesity  and  other chronic illnesses. However, this bill would impose a
significant new burden on school districts without any funds to  support
it. As such, this cost will ultimately be shouldered by local taxpayers.
This  is  unacceptable,  especially  when  school districts already file
plans with the State Education Department detailing the programming they
provide in physical education.

  School districts must also already file a  building  condition  survey
report  every  five  years detailing the instructional facilities of the
school district and adequacy of space, which includes physical education
space.  Finally,  significant  state  resources  would  be  required  to
compile, review, analyze, and report all of the data collected from each
elementary school in every school district across the State.

  Since  no funds were appropriated for this purpose, it must be consid-
ered in the  context  of  the  annual  budget  negotiations.  For  these
reasons, I am constrained to veto this bill.

  The bill is disapproved.                    (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
